messages:
maya: seeing a weird latency stall pattern after the new FIFO tweak under high concurrency. not typical thrash — looks like memory climbs and then a sudden latency jump for ~200ms batches :thinking:

dan: can you paste the flamegraph or pprof? is this KV eviction or paging? FIFO might be reinsert-churning with long contexts

maya: quick paste from prod-pprof (sampled during spike):
```
cpu: 2.3s total
    40%  runtime     kvcache.go:452   (*KVShard).EvictBatch
    22%  cgo          kernel_select.c:128 memcpy_optimized
    15%  runtime     kvcache.go:213   (*KVShard).Reinsert
     8%  runtime     kvcache.go:312   (*KVShard).EvictLoop
     5%  serving     batching.go:89   batchDispatcher
```

maya: looks like EvictBatch -> Reinsert -> EvictLoop cycle. memory bump correlates with long-context requests (seq_len > 8k)

priya: also saw a correlation with kernel selection changes — new quant kernels reduce compute but change seq padding behavior which increases KV page size per entry. that can worsen fragmentation and make FIFO more likely to evict "hot" prefixes

simon: couple thoughts:
- FIFO can give correctness surprises if reinserts race with paging (evicted entry pointers recycled)
- LRU can be heavier on bookkeeping but might avoid catastrophic eviction of recently-used long-context prefixes

maya: interesting — i captured a repro on staging. small load test with measured long-context ratio 8% triggers the stall in ~3m. attaching minimal repro command:
```
# run from perf harness
./harness --qps 400 --seq-dist long=8 --backend redwood-staging:443 --kv-pages=dynamic
```

dan: ran the repro quickly — confirmed non-deterministic 2-5x latency tail spikes. I grabbed logs, snippet: 
```
[2024-11-02T14:22:41Z] shard=7 evict: dropped page id=0x1f3 latch=0
[2024-11-02T14:22:41Z] shard=7 reinsert: page id=0x1f3 reused for seq=12345
[2024-11-02T14:22:41Z] shard=7 access: missing page id=0x1f3 -> page fault
```

dan: that looks like a race: evict -> reuse -> concurrent access thinks it's still valid then faults and triggers sync load, blocking the request

simon: yeah that's the atomicity bug we chatted about last month. FIFO's simple counters can hide the window where an entry is logically evicted but pointer reused before other threads see new generation ID

eva: infra-bot: deploy queued for kv-fix branch at 2024-11-03T02:00:00Z :rocket:

infra-bot: deploy-bot: started deploy kv-fix -> canary group: runtime-shard-7

maya: great — the kv-fix branch has a quick guard: generation tag check + delayed reuse (50ms) to avoid immediate pointer reuse. curious if that adds measurable memory churn or latency

priya: I ran a perf pass on canary with generation checks + batching heuristic tweak (prefer smaller batches for long contexts). results: 95p latency improved ~30%, tail spikes reduced but overall mem use up ~6% under sustained long-context workload

maya: tradeoff seems acceptable if correctness preserved. key question: can we make FIFO safe with a cheap generation check and retain its lower bookkeeping cost vs full LRU?

dan: prototype suggests generation check + atomic CAS on metadata is enough. cost is a few extra atomics on insert/evict paths. I also measured kernel-selection effect: when we switched kernels earlier, per-entry KV size increased ~12% which moved working set over watermark sooner

simon: so combo of larger entries + FIFO reuse race = transient paging storms. mitigation plan:
1) short-term: deploy kv-fix (gen tags + delayed reuse) + batching tweak to reduce long-context batch size
2) mid-term: add adaptive entry-sizing to kernel selection so we consider KV footprint when choosing kernel/quant profiles
3) long-term: evaluate LRU hybrid for shards with >X long-context ratio

maya: agreed. I'll open a small RFC for the adaptive kernel selection to include KV footprint metric. Dan/Simon can we get a PR for the gen-tag fix and a simple canary rollout plan?

dan: will PR today with bench results and a 48h canary plan

eva: noted. I'll schedule the canary and alert thresholds (mem + 99.9p latency)

maya: thanks all. filing postmortem if canary shows improved behavior. leaving logs and repro in the thread. :eyes:
